definition: BELIE'VE, verb transitive. To credit upon the authority or testimony of another; to be persuaded of the truth of something upon the declaration of another, or upon evidence furnished by reasons, arguments, and deductions of the mind. BELIE'VE, verb intransitive. To have a firm persuasion of any thing. In Scripture use, to believe in or on Christ is to trust, place full confidence in, and rest upon Him with faith.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: DO, verb transitive or auxiliary; preterit tense Did; participle passive Done. To perform; to execute; to carry into effect; to exert labor or power for bringing any thing to the state desired, or to completion; to bring any thing to pass. Also, to practice or perform, as to do good or evil.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: ALSO, adverb. In like manner; likewise; too; in addition to something already mentioned.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: EVERY, adjective. Each individual of a whole collection; each one of all; all taken separately.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: FATHER, noun. He who begets a child; a male parent. In Scripture, used also for an ancestor, founder, protector, ruler, instructor, or one who sustains a fatherly relation.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: HAVE, verb transitive. To possess; to hold in possession or power; to enjoy; to contain; to be under necessity or obligation. Used also as an auxiliary verb.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: ONE, adjective. Single in number; individual; undivided; the same. As a noun, a single person or thing.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SAY, verb transitive. To utter or pronounce in words; to speak; to declare; to tell; to affirm.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SHALL, verb auxiliary. Used to express future action or event; command; promise; determination; or obligation, according to person and context.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SPEAK, verb intransitive. To utter words or articulate sounds; to express thoughts by words. As a transitive verb, to utter, pronounce, declare, or tell.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THERE, adverb. In that place; at that point; in that respect; opposed to here.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THEREOF, adverb. Of that; of it; from that; concerning that thing.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THING, noun. Whatever exists, or is conceived to exist, as a separate object; an event, act, matter, subject, or concern.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: UPON, preposition. On; resting on the top or surface; not under. In Scripture and older English, also used for against, concerning, or immediately after, according to context.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: BEGET, verb transitive. To procreate; to generate; to produce as an effect.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: BROTHER, noun. A male born of the same parents, or of one parent; also one closely united by affection, fellowship, nation, office, or faith.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: CAST, verb transitive. To throw; to fling; to send or drive by force; to put, place, or turn.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: DWELL, verb intransitive. To abide as a permanent resident; to inhabit; to live in a place; to continue.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: NONE, adjective or pronoun. Not one; not any; no person or thing.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: NOR, conjunction. A negative connective; and not; used after neither or another negative.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: OTHER, adjective. Not the same; different; additional; the remaining one of two or more.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SHEW, verb transitive. Older spelling of show; to exhibit to view; to make known; to declare; to prove.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SHOULD, verb auxiliary. Used to express duty, obligation, fitness, condition, expectation, or future action from a past point of view.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SURE, adjective. Certain; firm; stable; not liable to fail; worthy of confidence.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: TAKE, verb transitive. To receive; to seize; to lay hold of; to get into possession; to accept; to choose.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THUS, adverb. In this manner; in this way; to this degree or extent.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: TWO, adjective. One and one; twice one; the number next after one.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: UNTIL, preposition or conjunction. To; unto; as far as; before the time that; up to the time when.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: WHERE, adverb. At which place; in what place; to what place; in which respect.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: WHOM, pronoun. The objective case of who; used of persons as the object of a verb or preposition.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: WHY, adverb. For what reason or cause; on what account.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: YEA, adverb. Yes; truly; certainly; used to affirm, intensify, or introduce a stronger statement.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: CERTAIN, adjective. Sure; true; fixed; settled; not doubtful. Sometimes used for some particular person or thing not named.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: COMMANDMENT, noun. A command; a mandate; an order or precept given by authority, especially a divine precept.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: FORTY, adjective. Four times ten; the number next after thirty-nine.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: HONOUR, noun. Dignity; reputation; esteem; reverence; true nobleness of mind. As a verb, to revere, respect, or treat with due esteem.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: LABOUR, noun. Exertion of body or mind; toil; work. As a verb, to work; to toil; to exert one's powers.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: NEIGHBOUR, noun. One who lives near another; in Scripture and moral use, a fellow man whom we are bound to regard with kindness.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: REMNANT, noun. That which is left after a part is removed, destroyed, or used; a residue; the remainder.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SAKE, noun. Cause; account; regard; purpose; end. Used chiefly in phrases such as for the sake of.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THENCE, adverb. From that place; from that time; from that source.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THEREIN, adverb. In that; in that place, thing, matter, or respect.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THITHER, adverb. To that place; toward that place.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: THREESCORE, adjective. Three times twenty; sixty.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: WHITHER, adverb. To what place; to which place; to what point or end.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: WOE, noun. Grief; sorrow; misery; calamity. Also used as an exclamation of grief or warning.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: HO'LY, adjective. Properly, whole, entire or perfect, in a moral sense. Hallowed; consecrated or set apart to a sacred use. Applied to God, perfectly pure, immaculate and complete in moral character.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: LAW, noun. A rule, particularly an established or permanent rule, prescribed by the supreme power of a state to its subjects. In Scripture, the word is used for God's revealed will, commandments, doctrine, or the whole Old Testament revelation depending on context.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: PRAY, verb intransitive. To ask with earnestness or zeal, as for a favor or for something desirable; to entreat; to supplicate. In worship, to address the Supreme Being with solemnity and reverence, with adoration, confession of sins, supplication for mercy, and thanksgiving for blessings received.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: PRA'YER, noun. In a general sense, the act of asking for a favor, and particularly with earnestness. In worship, a solemn address to the Supreme Being, consisting of adoration, confession of sins, supplication for mercy and forgiveness, intercession for blessings on others, and thanksgiving for mercies and benefits.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SALVA'TION, noun. The act of saving; preservation from destruction, danger or great calamity. In theology, deliverance from sin and its consequences, and admission to eternal happiness through the redemption of Christ.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SANCTIFICA'TION, noun. The act of making holy; the act of consecrating or setting apart for a sacred purpose. In theology, the work of God's grace by which believers are renewed after the image of God and enabled to die unto sin and live unto righteousness.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SHEPHERD, noun. A man employed in tending, feeding and guarding sheep in the pasture. In Scripture, a pastor, ruler or spiritual keeper of God's people.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: SUPPLICA'TION, noun. Entreaty; humble and earnest prayer in worship. A petition offered with submission and reverence.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: TRANSGRES'SION, noun. The act of passing over or beyond any law, rule or command; violation of law or known duty; offence; crime; sin.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: TRUTH, noun. Conformity to fact or reality; exact accordance with that which is, has been, or shall be. In Scripture, divine verity, faithfulness, purity from falsehood, and the doctrine of the Gospel.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: VISION, noun. The act of seeing external objects; sight. In Scripture, a supernatural appearance, revelation, or representation made to the mind, especially to a prophet.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: ZI'ON, noun. A hill in Jerusalem and, by extension in Scripture, Jerusalem, the people of God, or the church in prophetic and devotional use.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language
